Notable for methodological care: the Gaussian copula is fitted on training subjects only and applied fold-wise, so augmentation cannot leak across the validation split, which is the failure mode most augmentation papers in this index do not address.

paper-scalable-threat-assessment-machine.summary: This paper proposes a cloud-native threat assessment framework for CI/CD DevSecOps pipelines built on a hybrid Transformer-GNN ensemble model, trained and evaluated on the CICIDS-2017 intrusion detection dataset, addressing class imbalance via focal loss and stratified sampling rather than synthetic oversampling. CTGAN is discussed in the related-work review of synthetic tabular data generation for cybersecurity but is explicitly excluded from the pipeline because inserting synthetic samples would disrupt the temporal coherence needed for Transformer-based sequence learning.
paper-scalable-threat-assessment-machine.needs: Full text not obtained; only abstract-level citing sentences available, so cannot confirm any deeper engagement beyond the stated exclusion of CTGAN.

paper-synthetic-generation-population-br.summary: This paper examines the use of synthetic data generation methods applied to population-based breast cancer registry data, assessing their potential and limitations for downstream survival-analysis applications. Based on the metadata available, the study appears to evaluate tabular synthetic data generation techniques in an oncology registry context. CTGAN is cited as a synthetic tabular data generation method relevant to this evaluation.
paper-synthetic-generation-population-br.needs: Full text not available; cannot confirm whether CTGAN was run as a generator, used as a baseline, or only cited in passing. Title suggests synthetic data generation is central to the study's aims, but role of CTGAN specifically is unverified.

paper-convergence-centric-engineering-ad.summary: This is a vision/framework paper, instantiated within the Horizon Europe AI-DAPT project, that proposes a reference architecture unifying synthetic data generation, model observability, and adaptive AI operations for trustworthy production AI systems, with qualitative assessment of impact in the health and energy sectors. Rather than running new experiments, it surveys and organizes existing tooling into pillars, naming SDV's CTGAN, TVAE, Gaussian Copula, and ParSynthesizer as the synthetic-data-generation components adopted within the framework, explicitly noting the novelty lies in the reference architecture rather than re-implementing these libraries. SDV's CTGAN (with its mode-specific normalization and conditional sampling), TVAE, Gaussian Copula, and ParSynthesizer are described as the toolkit used to generate synthetic tabular and sequential data (e.g., load profiles, patient vitals) within the proposed pipeline.
paper-convergence-centric-engineering-ad.needs: No experimental results or code are shown for SDV components; usage is described at the level of a proposed/adopted framework rather than demonstrated runs, so actual execution of SDV code cannot be fully confirmed from this evidence.

paper-what-decision-support-product-2026.summary: This paper proposes a Conditional Tabular Variational Autoencoder (CTVAE) that learns the conditional joint distribution of consumer attributes given product design features, enabling what-if simulation of hypothetical product line extensions from home-scan panel data on over 20,000 consumers and 746 soft drink products. The authors reimplement CTGAN and TVAE from Xu et al. (2019) themselves, describing their own decoder equations and mode-specific normalization, and use these reimplementations as baselines showing CTVAE outperforms both in predictive accuracy. CTGAN/TVAE's mode-specific normalization and conditional training strategy are the SDV-family concepts adopted and reimplemented as comparison baselines, not run via the sdv-dev library itself.
paper-what-decision-support-product-2026.needs: Not certain whether the sdv-dev package or an original from-scratch implementation was used for the CTGAN/TVAE baselines; the explicit derivation of decoder equations suggests reimplementation (port) rather than library use.

paper-beware-counter-intuitive-levels-20.summary: This brief report demonstrates that in omics datasets with strong feature intra-correlations, standard FDR-controlling methods like Benjamini-Hochberg can counter-intuitively report surprisingly high numbers of false positives, and recommends using synthetic null data (negative controls) alongside suited multiple-testing strategies to detect and mitigate this issue. The paper mentions generic synthetic data generation libraries in passing as including copula-based and deep generative models. SDV (the Synthetic Data Vault) is cited only in a bibliographic reference as an example of such a library, with no evidence it was run.

paper-ctvae-contrastive-tabular-variatio.summary: This paper proposes CTVAE, a Conditional Tabular Variational Autoencoder that integrates conditional VAE generation with contrastive learning to synthesize high-quality samples for both minority and majority classes in imbalanced tabular datasets, and shows it can be combined with SMOTE variants for improved classification performance across 16 public datasets. CTGAN is cited only as the source of the data preprocessing pipeline (handling numerical and categorical columns) that the authors adapt for their own model, not run as a baseline or generator in the experiments. CTGAN's mode-specific normalization approach is thus adopted in prose rather than executed.

paper-cascade-input-doubling-classifier-.summary: This paper proposes an input-doubling classifier for small-data binary classification in transplantology, using a Probabilistic Neural Network to expand the feature space of an augmented dataset before a second machine learning algorithm performs final classification, with hyperparameters tuned via Dual Annealing. The method is tested on a small allogeneic bone marrow transplant survival dataset and compared against several existing approaches. CTGAN is only cited in the reference list as prior work on modeling tabular data with conditional GANs, and is never run or engaged with in the body text.

paper-constrained-tabular-diffusion-fina.summary: This paper introduces Constrained Tabular Diffusion for Finance (CTDF), a training-free feasibility operator embedded in the reverse-diffusion sampling loop of a mixed-type tabular diffusion model (built on TabDiff), enforcing hard regulatory and business-logic constraints on synthetic financial records without post-hoc filtering. Experiments on housing-market and Lending Club datasets show CTDF achieves zero constraint violations while improving fidelity metrics over unconstrained baselines. CTGAN is included as one of several standard generative baselines against which CTDF's fidelity is benchmarked.
paper-constrained-tabular-diffusion-fina.needs: TVAE in the same tables is cited to a different, unrelated 2023 paper (Ishfaq et al., triplet-based VAE), not SDV's TVAE, so it was excluded from sdv_concept.

paper-tvae-semi-supervised-educational-2.summary: Introduces TVAE-SSL for educational data mining under scarce labels: a TVAE is trained on whatever labelled data exists, its samples are folded back in as additional *unlabelled* data, and a standard self-training loop with a random forest base learner runs on the enlarged pool — enlarging the sample without manufacturing label noise. TVAE is the whole mechanism and TVAE ships in SDV, but the abstract names no implementation, so whether the library was run is unconfirmed.
paper-tvae-semi-supervised-educational-2.needs: MDPI returns 403 to automated fetches; confirm whether the TVAE is SDV's TVAESynthesizer or a bespoke implementation.

paper-enhancing-tabular-generation-dual-.summary: This paper proposes DSDDPM, a Dual-Scale Diffusion Probabilistic Method that improves tabular data synthesis by modeling global dependencies at a coarse noise scale and local feature details at a fine scale during forward and backward diffusion. It is evaluated against several state-of-the-art tabular generators on benchmark datasets, showing gains in machine-learning efficacy and distributional fidelity. CTGAN is run as one of the comparison baselines, with its training time and ML-efficiency score reported against DSDDPM's.
paper-enhancing-tabular-generation-dual-.needs: Not explicit whether the sdv-dev CTGAN package or an independent reimplementation was used to produce the reported training-time/MLE numbers.

paper-fuelvision-multimodal-fusion-multi.summary: FuelVision fuses Landsat-8 optical imagery, Sentinel-1 and PALSAR SAR data, and terrain features with an ensemble of deep learning, decision tree, and gradient-boosting models to map landscape-scale wildland fuels (Scott and Burgan 40) at near-real-time resolution, validated on the 2021 Dixie and Caldor fires. To overcome scarce FIA ground-truth plots, the authors generate pseudo-labeled and fully synthetic training data and compare five synthesizers -- TVAE, CTGAN, SMOTE, CGAN, and a Gaussian Copula Synthesizer -- trained through the Synthetic Data Vault library and scored with SDMetrics quality reports, ultimately selecting CTGAN's output to augment California FIA training data for the final ensemble model.

paper-financial-generation-utilizing-gra.summary: This paper proposes FNet, a module that augments GAN-based tabular synthesizers to preserve degree-centrality network structure in financial transaction data, addressing the failure of standard tabular GANs to capture account-level graph properties. The authors run CTGAN and CopulaGAN as baseline synthetic data generators on real online-transfer and ATM-transfer datasets, then combine each with FNet (CTGAN-FNet, CopulaGAN-FNet) and evaluate fraud-detection performance and utility metrics against the unmodified baselines. CTGAN and CopulaGAN, both from the SDV library, are run unmodified as the core generators that the whole empirical evaluation and proposed FNet extension build on top of.
paper-financial-generation-utilizing-gra.needs: Whether FNet modifies CTGAN/CopulaGAN's internal training loop (derivative_work) or is applied as a separate pre/post-processing stage (api_user) is not fully explicit in the extracted text; treated as api_user per the compound-name composition rule.

paper-generating-synthetic-locally-estim.summary: This paper introduces the Local Resampler (LR), a k-nearest-neighbour-based synthetic data generation method implemented in the Python package synloc, and formally shows that its NN variant systematically underrepresents outliers, giving built-in disclosure control. It compares LR's two variants against synthpop and other established synthesizers across simulated and real datasets on utility and privacy trade-offs. SDV is cited and its package is run as one of the benchmark methods evaluated against the proposed Local Resampler, described as including copula- and deep-learning-based techniques.
paper-generating-synthetic-locally-estim.needs: Unclear which specific SDV synthesizer(s) (e.g., GaussianCopula, FAST_ML preset) were run; 'FAST ML' appears in results tables and may correspond to SDV's FastML preset but this is not explicitly confirmed in the visible text.

paper-generative-tabular-synthesis-2025.summary: This PAKDD 2025 survey reviews tabular data synthesis (TDS) methods tailored to public-sector applications, categorizing statistical, machine-learning, deep-learning and LLM-based generators and their evaluation metrics along utility, fidelity and privacy dimensions, and proposing future research directions for government data use. It surveys CopulaGAN, CTGAN and TVAE in a comparison table and names SDMetrics among existing evaluation tools, without running any of them. SDV is cited only as the source paper for CopulaGAN and (mis-cited) for SDMetrics, engaged with descriptively rather than executed.
paper-generative-tabular-synthesis-2025.needs: Reference [28] is used inconsistently for both CopulaGAN and SDMetrics, apparently a citation-numbering error in the source PDF; treated as given, not corrected.

paper-machine-learning-driven-prediction.summary: This conference paper builds a prostate cancer prediction system that stratifies grade-7 Gleason score 3+4 versus 4+3 samples using multi-omics data (DNA methylation, gene expression, copy number alteration) and gene mutation profiles, combined with dimensionality reduction, autoencoders, and classifiers such as XGBoost. To address severe class imbalance between the two Gleason subtypes, the authors describe using 'a custom Conditional Tabular Generative Adversarial Network (CTGAN)' to generate synthetic minority-class samples, explaining its generator/discriminator behavior in their own prose rather than naming a package. CTGAN's generator-discriminator design is adopted as a custom-built synthetic oversampling method for the minority class, one preprocessing step among several in the classification pipeline.
paper-machine-learning-driven-prediction.needs: The paper calls its model a 'custom' CTGAN and describes generic generator/discriminator behavior rather than citing the sdv-dev package, constructor parameters, or an import; it is unclear whether they reimplemented CTGAN from scratch (port) or ran the SDV/ctgan library and merely called it 'custom' for their dataset.

paper-predicting-coronary-artery-disease.summary: This paper develops a CAD diagnosis pipeline on the Z-Alizadeh Sani dataset that combines XGBoost/Random-Forest ensemble feature selection with grid- and random-search-tuned classifiers (SVM, RF, LR, XGBoost, MLP), aiming to improve early detection of coronary artery disease under severe class imbalance. Three oversampling techniques -- SMOTE, ADASYN, and CT-GAN -- are systematically compared to rebalance the training folds, with ADASYN found to substantially outperform CT-GAN and SMOTE. CTGAN, described as a GAN-based conditional tabular data generator, is run as one of three oversampling baselines and is shown to underperform and even hurt classifier accuracy on this small clinical dataset.
paper-predicting-coronary-artery-disease.needs: No specific library/package name or constructor parameters are given for CT-GAN, so it is unclear whether the sdv-dev CTGAN package or a custom reimplementation was run; treated as baseline_only given the comparative framing.

paper-predictive-framework-cervical-canc.summary: This paper proposes DyFAGNN, a dynamic feature aggregation graph neural network for predicting cervical cancer brachytherapy fractionation mode, using a GPT-2 based generative model plus SMOTE/ADASYN balancing to overcome clinical data scarcity from 1271 patients. The synthetic-data pipeline is evaluated against several tabular generative baselines to justify the GPT-2 approach. CTGAN is run as one comparison benchmark against the authors' GPT-2 generator, with its Gaussian-mixture mode-specific encoding of numerical data noted in related work.

paper-privpetal-relational-synthesis-per.summary: This paper proposes PrivPetal, a differentially private relational data synthesis method that avoids generating join keys by flattening a relational schema into a 'permutation relation' and synthesizing it via a refined Markov random field mechanism, decomposing the result back into base relations. It is evaluated against prior DP synthesis methods including PrivLava on real datasets and the TPC-H benchmark, showing improved aggregate query accuracy. CTGAN appears only as a bibliographic citation in the reference list, with no engagement in the body text.

paper-timehr-image-time-series-2025.summary: This paper proposes TimEHR, a GAN-based model that treats irregularly sampled EHR time series as 2D images, using two conditional GANs to jointly generate missingness masks and their corresponding values. Experiments on three real-world EHR datasets show TimEHR outperforms prior methods on fidelity, utility, and privacy metrics. Within its pipeline, CTGAN is run to generate the static (non-time-series) patient variables conditioned on the label, feeding into the main image-based generators.

paper-generative-sequential-generation-m.summary: This paper proposes a five-step AI-based Monte Carlo simulation framework that trains generative AI models on real input data (e.g., action sequences from process data) to produce more realistic synthetic data than traditional hand-crafted simulations, then evaluates statistical methods' performance on this synthetic data. It includes explicit synthetic-data-quality assessment and robustness checks comparing AI-based versus traditional simulation outcomes. The original SDV paper is cited as prior work on synthetic data generation, though the abstract does not specify whether an SDV synthesizer itself was run.
paper-generative-sequential-generation-m.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether an SDV-family synthesizer (e.g., PAR/DeepEcho) was actually executed or if the citation is purely background on synthetic data generation frameworks.

paper-technique-synthetic-generation-ass.summary: This paper proposes AASGAN, a method that combines the Asset Administration Shell (AAS) knowledge representation used for Industry 4.0 digital twins with a GAN-based synthetic data generator, aiming to let manufacturers share realistic but non-confidential equipment and spare-parts data across an OEM network. The authors convert AAS submodels into tabular form and train a generative model to produce fake records that mimic the real data's statistical properties, later validated with the table_evaluator package. The Python 'ctgan' library is used directly as the generator, fitting and sampling synthetic tabular records from the AAS-derived tables, making CTGAN the core synthesis engine of the whole empirical pipeline.
paper-technique-synthetic-generation-ass.needs: SDV itself is cited only as background ([15], a generic mention of the SDV project); the empirically run generator is the standalone 'ctgan' PyPI package, treated here as SDV-family per the ctgan component.

paper-doubly-structured-synthesis-time-2.summary: This paper proposes DS2 (Doubly Structured Data Synthesis), a novel method for generating synthetic time-series energy-use data that preserves both longitudinal rate-change structure and cross-sectional mean structure via calibration, aimed at addressing privacy concerns in energy datasets. The authors evaluate DS2 against two existing generative baselines, CTGAN and TTS-GAN, across metrics of data similarity, utility, and privacy on real household electricity datasets, showing DS2 outperforms both. CTGAN, described as employing a conditional GAN with mode-specific normalization and training-by-sampling, is run unmodified as one of two comparison baselines throughout the empirical evaluation.

paper-melanoma-ctgan-ensemble-fs-2024.summary: Combines ensemble feature selection with tabular augmentation to identify melanoma from dermoscopy-derived features on two small, imbalanced public datasets, then uses SHAP, bootstrap tests and UMAP to make the resulting models interpretable to clinicians. CTGAN is the augmenter throughout: it synthesizes rows in the extracted feature and embedding space at controlled imbalance ratios, and the paper's best reported results are the combination of ensemble feature selection, CTGAN and linear models.

paper-epistemic-parity-reproducibility-e.summary: This paper proposes 'epistemic parity,' an evaluation methodology for differentially private synthetic data that measures whether published empirical conclusions would change if researchers had used DP synthetic data instead of the original real data, applied by reproducing peer-reviewed studies and re-running them on DP synthetic datasets. Among the DP synthesizers discussed is PATECTGAN, described as relying on a conditional generative adversarial network tuned to tabular data with privacy constraints on the discriminator. CTGAN's conditional GAN design for tabular data is cited as the architectural basis for PATECTGAN, without indication that SDV's own CTGAN implementation was run.
paper-epistemic-parity-reproducibility-e.needs: Full text not obtained; unclear whether CTGAN/PATECTGAN was actually run in the reproducibility experiments or only described as prior architecture.

paper-evaluating-temporal-fidelity-synth.summary: This paper proposes a comprehensive evaluation framework for assessing temporal fidelity in synthetic time-series Electronic Health Records, extending temporal clustering, time-series similarity measures, Sample Entropy, and trend analysis to compare real and synthetic EHRs generated by TimeGAN and EHR-M-GAN. The empirical work evaluates these two sequential generators against real MIMIC-III data and a random baseline, focusing on patient groupings, temporal dynamics, predictability, and directional change. CTGAN is cited only in passing as an example of GAN work addressing challenges of modelling mixed continuous/discrete data types, and is neither run nor engaged with further.
paper-evaluating-temporal-fidelity-synth.needs: Full text not obtained; unclear whether any synthetic EHR generator used in the actual experiments is CTGAN-based or unrelated (e.g., a sequence-specific model).

paper-generating-realistic-tabular-large.summary: This paper proposes Pred-LLM, an LLM-based tabular data generator that uses a novel permutation strategy during fine-tuning and feature-conditional sampling to jointly capture correct feature-class correlations, then generates labels via prompting. It is evaluated against 10 SOTA baselines across 20 datasets on downstream classification/regression tasks, quality, diversity, and privacy metrics. CTGAN, TVAE, and CopulaGAN (SDV's tabular synthesizers) are run as baseline generators throughout the experiments, with CTGAN reported as the best-performing GAN-based baseline.

paper-insights-generation-synthetic-enab.summary: This conference paper explores using SDV's Gaussian Copula Synthesizer to expand a small (58-patient) Heart Rate Variability dataset for Atrial Fibrillation research into a 1,000-record synthetic dataset, addressing both limited sample size and patient privacy concerns. The authors build an SDV single-table metadata object, fit the GaussianCopula synthesizer on the real data, and validate the synthetic output using SDV's evaluate_quality function and statistical tests. SDV's GaussianCopula synthesizer, metadata schema, and quality report are the core tools that generate and validate all synthetic data in the study.
paper-insights-generation-synthetic-enab.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether SDV software was actually run or only cited as background reference.

paper-leveraging-artificial-intelligence.summary: This conference paper addresses class imbalance in binary classification by combining SMOTE, GANs, and VAEs ("SMOTE-GAN-VAE") to generate synthetic minority instances, evaluated on a credit card fraud dataset using F0.5/F1/F2 scores. The combined approach is shown to outperform individual SMOTE, GAN, or VAE methods and a prior β-VAE filtered approach. The CTGAN paper is cited only as the reference for the generic GAN methodology used ([6], "Modeling tabular data using conditional gan"), with no CTGAN code run or discussed.
paper-leveraging-artificial-intelligence.needs: The GAN used in the actual SMOTE-GAN-VAE experiments is not specified as CTGAN; the citation appears to be a generic reference for GAN methodology rather than CTGAN specifically.

paper-performance-truthfulness-different.summary: This workshop paper examines whether differential-privacy-based anonymization techniques preserve the performance characteristics of a database workload, comparing DP algorithms (MST, AIM, PATE, PATE-CTGAN) against k-anonymity and hashing for cloud DB benchmarking. It reports practical limitations such as scaling and out-of-memory problems when dimensionality grows, and performance distortion for some queries. CTGAN, cited to Xu et al. 2019, is run (as part of the combined PATE-CTGAN and standalone GAN-based approach) as one of several evaluated synthetic-data-generation techniques, which the authors find suffers severe out-of-memory problems at scale.
paper-performance-truthfulness-different.needs: Unclear whether the sdv-dev CTGAN package or an independent implementation was run; no library import or parameter names are given in the evidence.

paper-privacy-preserving-blockchain-tran.summary: This paper proposes BTGM, a diffusion-based generative model for synthesizing blockchain transaction data that combines differential privacy with a two-stage diffusion process and VGM-based Row Modeling, aiming to balance detection accuracy with privacy protection. Validated on the Elliptic++ dataset, BTGM is shown to outperform CTGAN and STaSy on utility metrics and downstream classification while better resisting membership inference attacks. CTGAN's GAN-based architecture and its mode-specific normalization are described as prior art and run as a baseline generator, with its synthetic output and downstream performance compared directly against BTGM's.
paper-privacy-preserving-blockchain-tran.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether CTGAN was run via the sdv-dev package or reimplemented, nor detailed experimental setup.

paper-relative-frequency-rank-encoding-2.summary: This paper proposes a new encoding scheme for non-numerical network features (e.g., IP addresses, port numbers) that ranks values by frequency and maps them evenly into [0,1], improving unsupervised anomaly detection performance on datasets like CICIDS2017. To handle continuous network-flow features with multiple modes, the authors adopt the variational Gaussian mixture (VGM) idea from CTGAN's mode-specific normalization, implementing it in their own pipeline rather than running the SDV library. CTGAN's mode-specific normalization concept is cited and its VGM approach is adopted in prose, but the SDV code itself is never invoked.
paper-relative-frequency-rank-encoding-2.needs: Confirmed full-text finding: no SDV-family term appears outside the reference list/citation sentences, so this is adoption-in-prose, not library use.

paper-representation-debiasing-generated.summary: This paper proposes human-in-the-loop interaction approaches that let domain experts steer data augmentation algorithms to mitigate representation bias in datasets used for training ML models, and discusses how such expert-guided validation and refinement of generated samples can support user-centred AI systems. It is a conceptual/position paper with no reported experiments of its own. The Synthetic Data Vault is cited in passing to support the claim that augmented datasets can be made more balanced and representative, reducing bias in prediction models.

paper-residential-building-heating-load-.summary: This paper proposes TabNet-GAN, a hybrid deep learning model that combines the TabNet tabular learner with a GAN/CGAN-based data augmentation module to overcome the small size (768 records) of a residential heating-load dataset, reporting that the augmented TabNet model becomes competitive with classical ML baselines. In its background section it describes CTGAN's mode-specific normalization and conditional generator for handling multimodal, imbalanced tabular columns, citing Xu et al., but its own augmentation module is a custom GAN/CGAN implementation rather than the SDV package. CTGAN is discussed and its design elements are referenced as prior art rather than run.

paper-signal-quality-detection-mobile-20.summary: This conference paper from Orange Labs proposes an adapted GAN model, combined with the OverPy OpenStreetMap tool, to generate synthetic SNR (signal-to-noise ratio) values tied to real vehicle GPS traces, using opt-in Signal Map mobile-app data from Nice, France, in order to enrich mobile network QoS datasets while preserving user privacy. The authors describe CTGAN's design for modeling mixed continuous/discrete tabular data and explicitly adopt its proposed normalization approach as one of two normalization modes used inside their own custom GAN, without stating that the sdv-dev CTGAN package itself was run. CTGAN's mode-specific normalization is thus adopted conceptually into the authors' own model rather than executed via the SDV library, and SDMetrics is separately listed in the reference list (with version number) without described use in the text.
paper-signal-quality-detection-mobile-20.needs: SDMetrics is cited in the reference list with a specific version number (0.9.3) but no body passage confirms actual usage for evaluation; could not verify whether it was run.

paper-tramcol-diff-deepening-diffusion-2.summary: This paper proposes TRamCol-Diff, a diffusion-model-based tabular data generator for Medical Service Data that uses a random column rearrangement (TRamCol) strategy to help the model learn implicit inter-column relationships and improve synthetic data fidelity. It benchmarks TRamCol-Diff against NFlow, ADS-GAN, PATE-GAN, TVAE, CTGAN, and TabDDPM, reporting quantitative fidelity/utility metrics for each, and also tests TRamCol combined with each baseline. CTGAN and TVAE are run as two of several comparison generators against which the proposed diffusion model's performance is measured.
paper-tramcol-diff-deepening-diffusion-2.needs: Whether CTGAN/TVAE were run via the sdv-dev/ctgan package or the authors' own reimplementation is not specified in the evidence; marked baseline_only rather than api_user/port.

paper-shapley-feature-selection-method-2.summary: This paper proposes a class-based Shapley-value feature selection method within a Decision Tree-based clinical decision support system for classifying lung diseases (healthy, URTI, COPD, Pneumonia, Bronchiolitis) from lung sound recordings using PSD, MFCC, and statistical features. It shows that combining Shapley-based feature selection with a parallel ensemble of binary decision-tree classifiers improves classification performance over raw features or traditional Shapley use. TGAN (Xu & Veeramachaneni 2018) appears only as a bibliographic citation in a list of references for decision-tree-related work, with no engagement in the text.
paper-shapley-feature-selection-method-2.needs: The citation appears to be a mismatched/erroneous reference attached to a Decision Tree sentence, unrelated to the paper's actual content.

paper-advances-automatically-rating-trus.summary: This paper presents methods for rating the trustworthiness of black-box AI text-processing services (e.g., machine translators) from an independent stakeholder's perspective, drawing an analogy to nutritional labeling, and outlines a broader vision for causality-based, multimodal trust rating. It discusses how such ratings communicate risk to consumers without needing access to a service's source code or training data. The Synthetic Data Vault paper is cited only in the bibliography, with no engagement with SDV in the body text.
paper-advances-automatically-rating-trus.needs: The provided 'sentences in which this work cites an SDV paper' does not actually reference SDV content, suggesting a possible citation-matching artifact; treated as citation_only per settled finding.

paper-enhancing-public-research-citizen-.summary: This paper presents an empirical framework for generating and evaluating synthetic versions of citizen microdata held in New Zealand's Integrated Data Infrastructure (IDI), comparing multiple data-synthesis algorithms on statistical similarity, machine-learning utility, and privacy risk. It finds that distance-based methods like SMOTE offer the best accuracy/computational-cost tradeoff for the IDI setting and outlines opportunities for synthetic data in reproducibility, pilot analyses, and cross-domain research access. CTGAN is included among the evaluated data-synthesis algorithms as one of several generators benchmarked in the empirical comparison.
paper-enhancing-public-research-citizen-.needs: Full text not obtained; abstract only confirms CTGAN was one of several benchmarked algorithms, without detail on implementation (own reimplementation vs. sdv-dev/CTGAN package) or specific results.

paper-naturalfuzz-2023.summary: Argues that fuzzed inputs for big data analytics are unrealistic enough to be unhelpful downstream, and generates natural inputs from real data instead. SDV is the comparison the claim is stated against, with the authors reporting nine times more faults found at comparable input sizes; the entry records an adversarial result rather than a use.

paper-optimal-adjustment-sets-biomolecul.summary: Addresses which variables to condition on when estimating a causal effect in a biomolecular network that is only partially observed, showing that using every available variable can increase bias and variance, and selecting an adjustment set by simulating future datasets and comparing candidate sets on them. A tabular GAN attributed to Xu et al. is the simulator that step rests on, trained on historical observational data to approximate the true data-generating process, but the implementation run is Ashrapov's third-party library rather than the SDV one.
paper-optimal-adjustment-sets-biomolecul.needs: Convention gap, and the second instance in this lane: a paper runs a THIRD-PARTY REIMPLEMENTATION of CTGAN (Ashrapov's tabgan) as its production generator while crediting Xu et al. for the method. paper-llm-gan-energy-load-2024 in shard 95 does the same but only describes CTGAN in background, so citation_only 2 was uncontroversial there. Here the simulator is load-bearing for the paper's central procedure, which argues for importance 3, or for a separate treatment of third-party reimplementations alongside the third-party derivative question on paper-nft-data-trading-dpctgan-2025. Note the deduplication history: an independent curation of this work's preprint reached api_user 3 on identical evidence, so a ruling here also settles that disagreement

paper-robust-pulse-shape-discrimination-.summary: This paper proposes a pulse shape discrimination algorithm for classifying neutron and gamma pulses in radiation detectors, using scalogram features from the Continuous Wavelet Transform, 2D PCA for dimensionality reduction, and Canonical Correlation Analysis for classification, reporting improved accuracy over state-of-the-art PSD methods. The SDV paper is cited only in passing as general motivation for why machine learning applications increasingly use synthetic rather than real data for training and testing classifiers.
paper-robust-pulse-shape-discrimination-.needs: Full text not available; cannot confirm whether SDV tools were ever actually used in this radiation-detector pulse classification work or if the citation is purely rhetorical.

paper-speaker-anonymization-generative-a.summary: This paper proposes a GAN-based approach to speaker anonymization that generates a pool of synthetic fake speaker identities, avoiding the risk of matching anonymized speech to a real existing speaker's identity. Several GAN architectures were tested for generating these identity vectors, evaluated on speech naturalness and linguistic content preservation metrics. CTGAN, SDV's conditional tabular GAN, was run as one of several candidate generators and reportedly achieved the best performance among them.
paper-speaker-anonymization-generative-a.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether the sdv-dev CTGAN package was used directly or a reimplementation, nor authors' institutional affiliations.

paper-synthetic-generation-artificial-in.summary: This paper reports the development and clinical validation of a synthetic-data generation pipeline for myelodysplastic syndromes and AML, producing synthetic cohorts of 7,133 patients (clinical, genomic, treatment and outcome data) that were shown to accelerate discovery of molecular classification/scoring systems and to recapitulate a clinical trial's endpoints. The generative core is described as 'a conditional Wasserstein's tabular GAN with gradient penalty,' an architecture the authors built themselves, citing CTGAN as its basis while modifying its loss with a Wasserstein critic and gradient penalty. CTGAN's conditional tabular GAN design is thus adapted into a new generator rather than run as the sdv-dev package, forming the load-bearing generative method behind the entire empirical programme.
paper-synthetic-generation-artificial-in.needs: Full architecture details are not in the excerpted text; unclear whether this is a genuinely novel loss modification (derivative_work) or simply a from-scratch reimplementation of CTGAN's conditional design (port). paper-tabular-gan-oversampling-imbalance.summary: This conference paper investigates GAN-based oversampling for class-imbalanced survival (time-to-event) prediction, comparing four tabular GAN methods against traditional oversampling techniques (SMOTE, SVMSMOTE, BorderlineSMOTE) across real-world and simulated medical datasets. It finds that traditional resampling methods generally outperform GAN-based ones on both synthetic sample fidelity and downstream survival prediction accuracy. CTGAN is one of the four GAN baselines run and evaluated as a minority-class oversampler, described as using mode-specific normalization and conditional-generator/training-by-sampling techniques.

paper-efficient-insights-discovery-condi.summary: This SIGMOD demo paper presents Electra, a system combining automated data-insight discovery with a machine-learning driven approximate query processing (AQP) engine that uses a conditional generative model to synthesize a small sample of rows matching a query, enabling low-latency accurate approximate answers for complex multi-predicate queries. Electra's own conditional generative approach is benchmarked against several state-of-the-art AQP baselines, including VAE-AQP, DeepDB, and VerdictDB. CTGAN is cited and run as one of the baseline generative models Electra is compared against on the Flights dataset for approximation error.

paper-tutor-decision-rules-2022.summary: Trains neural networks on small tabular datasets by using decision rules as priors and synthesising extra data to train against. CTGAN is the generator its own synthesis framework is measured against.

paper-tabular-learning-traffic-event-202.summary: This paper proposes a tabular learning framework using the TabNet model to predict traffic events by integrating social traffic data, with model interpretability analysis to assess the importance of external traffic factors for autonomous driving and traffic planning applications. CTGAN is mentioned only in passing within a related-work discussion of prior deep neural network architectures for tabular data, alongside TabNN, without being run or evaluated. SDV's CTGAN is cited only as one of several prior tabular DNN architectures that did not achieve overwhelming performance.

paper-utility-metrics-synthetic-health-2.summary: Tests whether the utility metrics people report for synthetic health data can actually rank competing generators the way a downstream modeller would, by generating synthetic versions of 30 heterogeneous health datasets, fitting logistic regression prediction models on real and synthetic data, and checking which metric orders the generators consistently with the observed AUROC and AUPRC gaps. A multivariate Hellinger distance computed over a Gaussian copula representation of the real and synthetic joint distributions comes out best, and an aggregate of several metrics adds almost nothing over it. Three generative models supply the variation the metrics are ranked against, and the first of them is the conditional GAN of Xu et al., the other two being a differentially private Bayesian network and sequential synthesis with decision trees. SDV's generator is therefore run across all 30 datasets as one of three arms in a study whose subject is the metrics rather than the generators.

paper-federated-qoe-ensemble-2020.summary: Addresses the problem that quality-of-experience models need labelled data pooled across subjects while data-protection regulation blocks sharing the local datasets, and proposes synthesising shareable substitutes with an ensemble of Bayesian network models trained at each site. CTGAN is the tabular-GAN prior art the design departs from: the paper credits it with addressing multi-modality and varying distribution in continuous attributes through conditional GANs and preprocessing, then declines to adopt it, judging the per-dataset manual work and the tuning burden across its component algorithms too heavy for the QoE datasets in hand.

paper-performance-comparison-multi-class.summary: This conference paper compares SVM classification performance when the training data class imbalance in the KDD Cup 99 intrusion detection dataset is corrected using different oversampling methods: random SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE, ADASYN, and a GAN-based approach. CTGAN is trained and run as the oversampling generator, and its output is shown to yield the lowest data-duplication rate and the highest F1 score (90.98%) compared to the SMOTE-family baselines, with statistical significance confirmed via Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. CTGAN, described with its variational Gaussian mixture mode-specific normalization, is the load-bearing generator whose synthetic minority samples drive the paper's headline result.
paper-performance-comparison-multi-class.needs: Not fully clear whether the sdv-dev CTGAN package or a custom reimplementation was run; hyperparameters given (two hidden layers, ReLU, Adam) do not match the standard CTGAN constructor parameter names, so exact provenance is uncertain.

paper-distribution-driven-embedded-synth.summary: This paper proposes the concept of a 'shadow database' derived from a production database to preserve its distribution properties, and presents an embedded synthetic data generation tool implemented as SQL procedures for RDBMS, using data distribution histograms rather than raw data. It contrasts its distribution-driven, embedded approach with prior generators including query-aware and application-oriented tools. SDV's Gaussian Copula Process approach to learning data distributions is discussed and cited in related work as a differing prior method, not run or extended.

paper-synthetic-generators-promote-open-.summary: This conference paper argues that synthetic data generators can enable open, shareable datasets for higher-education learning-analytics research despite privacy restrictions on real student data, comparing synthetic to original data characteristics and demonstrating use of the synthetic data to train a common learning-analytics algorithm. In its related-work discussion of prior synthetic data systems it cites the Synthetic Data Vault (SDV), describing it as 'another system for creating synthetic data' used to generate five publicly available datasets, without adopting or running it in the authors' own pipeline.

paper-gactgan-swag-2026.summary: Places a Bayesian posterior over a tabular GAN's generator weights without the memory cost of the Markov chain approach, by collecting a running mean and low-rank plus diagonal covariance of the generator weights during training with Stochastic Weight Averaging-Gaussian and sampling from that Gaussian at synthesis time, and reports on five national census tables plus Adult and a churn dataset that the result sits higher on the utility axis of a risk-utility map without a matching rise in attribute-disclosure risk. The model is a named CTGAN variant: SWAG is integrated into CTGAN's own generator, the paper's ablations run averaging-only and several covariance ranks against unmodified CTGAN and a Markov-chain BayesCTGAN, and the implementation is published as a CTGAN fork.

preprint-compass-unified-decision-intell.summary: COMPASS is a modular, interactive decision-intelligence engine for HPC configuration selection that turns user queries (recommend, reconfigure, what-if) into ML tasks, quantifies the trustworthiness of its suggestions, and is validated against analytical ground truth, published findings, and real hardware. It is compared against autotuners, predictive models, and generative modeling baselines including CTGAN, GAN, GReaT, and diffusion models on tabular configuration generation tasks. CTGAN is run as one of several generative baselines in the paper's comparison table, evaluated against COMPASS on recommendation quality, training/inference speed, and reconstruction accuracy.

preprint-cross-domain-feature-expansion-.summary: This paper proposes MedKGTab, a knowledge-injected framework that fuses data-driven statistical priors with the SPOKE biomedical knowledge graph to infer uncollected biomedical features across medical cohorts, using a row-column dual-attention mechanism operating on raw tabular data. It is evaluated against specialized tabular generation models and medical LLMs on intra- and cross-cohort feature expansion tasks. The SDV suite's Column Distribution and Inter-Column Relationship metrics are run to quantify cross-cohort generative fidelity, and CTGAN/TVAE are cited in related work as prior deep generative baselines for mixed-type tabular data.

paper-membership-disclosure-kde-2026.summary: Proposes a membership inference framework for tabular synthetic data that fits kernel density estimators to member and non-member distance distributions, recovering the probabilistic output and ROC analysis of shadow-model attacks without retraining any generator, and shows through ROC analysis that datasets judged safe on average accuracy can still leak badly at low false positive rates. CTGAN and TVAE are two of the six generators whose output the attack is run against across four datasets, both trained on the real data through the SynthCity framework.

preprint-remia-powerful-efficient-altern.summary: This paper introduces ReMIA, a practical privacy-risk metric for synthetic tabular data generators that requires only two generator training runs and modest auxiliary data, offering sensitivity comparable to state-of-the-art shadow-modeling membership inference attacks at a fraction of the cost. The authors benchmark ReMIA and competing privacy/fidelity metrics across multiple tabular datasets and a set of eleven synthetic data generators. CTGAN and TVAE, both from the CTGAN NeurIPS 2019 paper, are included among these eleven generators as evaluation subjects, run via the reprosyn and synthcity implementation libraries rather than the original SDV-family package; the earlier Synthetic Data Vault paper is cited only in passing among related generative-modeling approaches.

preprint-sherpa-privacy-preserving-multi.summary: This paper proposes a multi-party private set union (PSU) protocol for vertical federated learning that aligns records across parties without revealing intersection membership, supporting both exact and typo-tolerant noisy matching. It proves correctness and privacy, analyzes communication and computational complexity, and formalizes a universal index mapping across parties' local records. To fill in features missing for non-overlapping records after alignment, the authors describe using the Synthetic Data Vault, detailing its Gaussian Copula and CTGAN backends (including mode-specific normalization and the conditional sampling vector) as the intended synthetic-data generation mechanism, without showing an experimental run of the library.

preprint-adversarial-causal-tuning-reali.summary: This paper introduces Adversarial Causal Tuning (ACT), a methodology for causal-model tuning that searches over causal discovery pipelines and adversarial discriminators to select the causal model best matching a real time-series dataset, enabling realistic simulation, what-if scenario generation, and causal benchmark creation. It is evaluated on real, semi-synthetic, and synthetic time-series datasets against non-causal generative baselines. In these experiments, SDV's CPAR (sequential PAR model) is run as one of several comparison baselines alongside CausalTime and TimeVAE.

preprint-assessing-generative-models-str.summary: This preprint proposes new statistical methods for directly assessing synthetic tabular data quality by examining inter-column dependencies (marginal, pairwise, and higher-order joint cumulants) rather than relying on train-synthetic-test-real utility metrics. Applying these methods to GPT-2 (few-shot and fine-tuned) and a GAN baseline across Adult, Breast Cancer, and Credit datasets, the authors find that none of the generative methods reproduce the real data's higher-order dependency structure. CTGAN, run via its implementation from the Synthetic Data Vault, serves as the GAN baseline compared against the LLM-based approaches throughout the empirical evaluation.

preprint-boosting-knnclassifier-performa.summary: This preprint proposes an Opposition-Based Learning (OBL) data transformation framework that generates synthetic 'opposite' samples to augment training data, testing three OBL variants combined with K-Nearest Neighbors across 26 heterogeneous, high-dimensional datasets to improve classification performance. CTGAN is cited only in the reference list, as a specific example of generative models for tabular data, with no evidence it was implemented or run.

preprint-privacy-preserving-dataset-comb.summary: This paper introduces SecureKL, a secure multi-party computation protocol for privately evaluating dataset divergence between organizations before committing to data-sharing collaborations, applied to ICU mortality prediction across hospitals and income prediction across states. The related-work discussion on synthetic data cites CTGAN and TVAE as examples of tabular generative methods that learn complex distributions while preserving feature correlations. CTGAN and TVAE are mentioned only as background citations, not run or benchmarked in the protocol.

preprint-synthetic-ratemaking-imputation.summary: This preprint benchmarks Multivariate Imputation by Chained Equations (MICE) against deep generative models -- Variational Autoencoders and Conditional Tabular GANs, plus hybrid CTGAN-AE and CTGAN-MICE variants -- for generating synthetic actuarial (insurance claims) data, assessing marginal and multivariate fidelity, GLM coefficient consistency, and data-augmentation effects on claim-count prediction. The authors conclude MICE-based methods offer competitive fidelity with lower implementation complexity than deep generative approaches. CTGAN is run explicitly as "implementation of Xu et al. (2019) available in the sdv library for Python", used as one of several generative benchmarks alongside its AE- and MICE-augmented hybrids.

The pipeline is built on Gaussian copulas chosen specifically to preserve associations across high-resolution peptidomics variables, so SDV's copula is selected for a dependence-preservation property rather than convenience.

preprint-balanced-mixed-type-tabular-202.summary: This paper introduces a fairness-aware tabular diffusion model that incorporates sensitive-attribute guidance to generate balanced synthetic data with improved demographic parity and equalized odds compared to prior tabular synthesis methods. It evaluates its diffusion-based generator against several baselines including GAN- and VAE-based tabular synthesizers on datasets such as Adult, Bank, and COMPAS. CTGAN and TVAE, described as GAN- and VAE-based tabular synthesis approaches with 'user-friendly implementation' credited to the SDV paper (Patki et al., 2016), are run as two of several comparison baselines that the proposed method is reported to generally outperform.

preprint-federated-learning-gans-synthet.summary: This preprint studies imbalanced learning for weather prediction (e.g., rare severe-weather events) under both centralized and federated learning settings, comparing GAN-based and SMOTE-based data augmentation techniques to improve classifier performance on tabular weather data. The authors report federated learning combined with GAN/SMOTE oversampling improves accuracy and generalization on minority-class weather events. The paper's metadata indicates it cites the CTGAN paper, but no CTGAN or SDV-related passage could be located in the extracted full text, so the nature of this citation is unclear.

preprint-latent-imitator-generating-natu.summary: This paper proposes Latent Imitator (LIMI), a black-box fairness-testing framework that imitates a target model's decision boundary in the semantic latent space of a GAN to generate more natural individual discriminatory test instances, improving effectiveness, efficiency, and naturalness over prior baselines and showing that retraining on generated samples improves individual and group fairness. CTGAN is adopted as the GAN model trained on each tabular dataset (300 epochs, batch size 500) to provide the latent space LIMI operates on, and SDMetrics is used to implement the naturalness evaluation metric. CTGAN and SDMetrics are the SDV-family components run directly as the generator backbone and evaluation library underpinning the empirical study.

preprint-caleb-conditional-adversarial-l.summary: This paper proposes CALEB, a framework using Conditional GAN and Auxiliary Classifier GAN to simulate evolving social bot behavior and generate synthetic bot instances that augment training data for more adaptive bot detection on Twitter. The authors evaluate the fidelity of their synthetic data against real data and against ADASYN-generated data using two statistical similarity metrics. These metrics, the Kolmogorov-Smirnov test and continuous KL Divergence, are drawn from the Synthetic Data Vault's evaluation toolkit and run directly to score how closely the generated bot instances match the original distributions.

preprint-conditional-synthetic-generatio.summary: This preprint proposes generating conditional synthetic data to address severe class imbalance in personal thermal comfort datasets, using the authors' own conditional generative model (from Das et al. 2021b) to oversample under-represented 'Prefer Warmer'/'Prefer Cooler' classes and mimic the real data distribution for privacy-preserving sharing. CTGAN (Xu et al. 2019) is cited in the related work as prior art for modeling tabular data for synthetic generation, but the paper's own generator, not CTGAN, is run in the experiments. CTGAN is only cited, never executed.

preprint-generating-realistic-synthetic-.summary: The paper introduces graph-VAE, a method combining variational autoencoders with graph neural networks to synthesize realistic relational databases with multiple interconnected tables, evaluated on two public datasets for structural fidelity and privacy. It argues that prior deep generative approaches to tabular data generate only statistically independent rows and cannot handle complex relational structures. CTGAN and TGAN are named only in a string of citations for tabular-data generation methods, with no further engagement or use in the reported experiments.

preprint-utility-assessment-synthetic-ge.summary: This paper empirically investigates how different synthetic data generation methods and synthesis parameters affect data utility, comparing a priori metrics against a posteriori analysis accuracy across census-type (Adult, Polish) and other (Avila) datasets, using primarily decision-tree and Synthpop-based synthesizers. In its related-work discussion it describes a prior study that compared four data synthesizers including Data-Synthesizer, Synthpop variants, and the Synthetic Data Vault (SDV), finding Synthpop Non-parametric performed best overall. SDV is only cited as one synthesizer used in a related paper's comparison, not run in this work's own experiments.

In a passage on data quality remedies, the authors mention synthetic data generation tools alongside SMOTE as a way to address missing data and outlier problems. TGAN (Xu and Veeramachaneni, 2018) is cited only in passing as providing 'a convenient solution for missing data imputation and outlier treatment,' with no experiments run using it.

preprint-permuteattack-counterfactual-ex.summary: This paper proposes PermuteAttack, a genetic-algorithm-based counterfactual example generator for tabular data, aimed at explaining and stress-testing machine learning credit scorecard models used in retail credit risk. The method perturbs discrete and categorical tabular features to produce adversarial counterfactuals that reveal model weaknesses without requiring gradient access. TGAN is cited only in the bibliography as prior work on synthesizing tabular data with generative adversarial networks, with no evidence it was run or engaged with in the body text.

The work is framed as an alternative to GANs and VAEs that avoids strong distributional assumptions and adversarial training instability. The Synthetic Data Vault paper (Patki, Wedge & Veeramachaneni 2016) appears only in the reference list, with no engagement with SDV's library or methods in the body text.
